solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Hand over alcohol -- it'll help when leaving the EU (8)

definitions.text: it'll help when leaving the EU

blocks.note: to pass something is to hand it over

annotation.surface: A cheeky bribe of booze to smooth a departure from the European Union.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests slipping a bottle to a customs officer; in fact the two opening ideas are simply joined, and the rest is a whimsical description of the document.
annotation.definitionFit: A whimsical description by function rather than a synonym: after Brexit, Britons need the document stamped at EU borders.

entries.clue: Shame about a Republican's correspondence (6)

indicators.note: 'About' in the sense of around: the shame word stands round the A and R.

annotation.surface: Disgrace surrounding a political party member's letters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' pretends to mean letters, but here it means equivalence or matching, as between two currencies.
annotation.definitionFit: Parity is equality, and the close correspondence between two values, as with currencies at par, is a matter of parity.

entries.clue: Thought son cut speed round the bend (9)

indicators.note: 'Round the bend' is slang for crazy, and crazed letters don't stay in their order.

annotation.surface: A driver's son slowed down as he took a corner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round the bend' reads as a stretch of road, which is why it hides so well after 'cut speed'.
annotation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb: 'I suspected as much' means 'I thought as much', a close synonym.

entries.clue: Her pilot, up in the air, wanting love? This could help (7)

indicators.note: Things up in the air are tossed about and come down in a new order.
'Wanting' means lacking, so the letters of her pilot go without the O.

blocks.note: love = O, zero in tennis; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A woman whose airborne pilot is lonely, and something that might win him over.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue ends by pointing at itself: the answer is exactly what someone wanting love might need. 'Up in the air' fits the pilot but stirs the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a philtre is a love potion, the kind of thing that helps someone whose love life is lacking.

entries.clue: Compass needle moving right to the start (5)

indicators.note: R is right, and moving it to the start takes the last letter round to the front.

blocks.note: to needle someone is to anger them

annotation.surface: A compass needle swinging round to point back to where it began.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compass needle' looks like one object; split it into definition and wordplay. Nothing is lost in the move: the R leaves the end and rejoins at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Compass is an old sense meaning extent or scope, as in 'within the compass of' a plan or a singer's voice.

entries.clue: Evil spirits disturbed Slough (6)

indicators.note: Something disturbed has been knocked out of place, so the letters are rearranged.

annotation.surface: Evil spirits have unsettled the town of Slough.
annotation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, much mocked in poetry and on TV; the capital letter makes it look like a place, not raw letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Ghouls come from Arabic folklore as grave-robbing demons, so they fit evil spirits as a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Composer with sign of hesitation -- piece could be removed from here (7)

definitions.text: piece could be removed from here

blocks.note: Gustav Holst, composer of The Planets

annotation.surface: A composer hesitates over which piece of music to drop from a programme.
annotation.walkthrough: With a composer about, 'piece' means a work of music; here it is slang for a gun.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: 'piece' is gangster slang for a handgun, and a holster is where it is drawn from.

entries.clue: Golf club missing head, say (5)

indicators.note: A word's head is its first letter, and here that letter is missing.

annotation.surface: A putter whose head has come off, as a golfer might describe it.
annotation.walkthrough: A club missing its head is a real mishap on the course; here the head is only the first letter P.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to utter a word is to say it aloud.

entries.clue: Shooting pain's beginning in gardening activity (8)

indicators.note: A word's beginning is its first letter.
'In' places the P inside the gardening word.

annotation.surface: A sharp pain that started while the gardener was at work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shooting pain' reads as one phrase; split it after the first word, which means moving fast, as a shooting star does.
annotation.definitionFit: Shooting past something means moving fast, the same idea as speeding in a car.

entries.clue: Bird food (8)

blocks.note: bird is British rhyming slang (bird-lime = time) for a prison sentence

annotation.surface: Seed for the birds.
annotation.walkthrough: Both 'bird' and 'porridge' are British slang for time served in prison; the surface wants a feathered creature.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: porridge is a breakfast of oats, and British slang for a prison sentence, which 'bird' also means.

entries.clue: Euro result isn't fantastic -- embracing America is a risky game to play (7,8)

indicators.note: Fantastic in the sense of fanciful: the letters are reshaped into something unreal.
Arms embracing someone go round them, so the rearranged letters wrap round the A.

annotation.surface: A disappointing Euro football result, and taking on the Americans is a gamble.
annotation.walkthrough: The Euros are the European football championship, so the surface is a sports report; the fodder spans most of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: the game of spinning a revolver with one bullet and firing at your own head.

entries.clue: Regularly acts in that place (7)

indicators.note: Taking letters at regular intervals keeps every other one.
'In' puts those letters inside the word for that place.

blocks.note: the first and third letters of Acts

annotation.surface: Somebody who performs in a certain venue on a regular basis.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: read straight, it describes the building where plays are acted night after night.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the whole clue describes a playhouse, where performers act on a regular schedule.

entries.clue: Went to bed really missing friend and bored (7)

indicators.note: 'Missing' means going without, so the friend's letters are taken out.

annotation.surface: Somebody went to bed missing a friend and fed up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Missing friend' sounds like loneliness; the friend is a word that sits neatly inside the one before it.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Retire' in the old sense of withdrawing for the night, so 'went to bed' matches in tense.

entries.clue: Is losing first hair? Editor's anxious (8)

indicators.note: The word loses its first letter.

blocks.note: a tress is a lock of hair

annotation.surface: An editor fretting about losing hair.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether someone is balding; 'losing first' only removes one letter from the short word before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A modern synonym: someone stressed is tense and worried, as is someone anxious.

entries.clue: Nip inside branch for business chat (4,4)

indicators.note: 'Inside' puts the nip word within the branch word.

blocks.note: to nip or hop somewhere is to go quickly
a stalk is a plant's branch or stem

annotation.surface: Popping into a local branch of a firm to discuss work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Branch' suggests a bank or shop outlet, which fits the business chat; it is a plant stem.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'talking shop' is discussing your work, so shop talk is chat about business.

entries.clue: Be in power shower, by the sound of it (5)

indicators.note: Judged by its sound, not its spelling: the word heard is spelt another way.

annotation.surface: Standing under a power shower.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Power shower' is a strong bathroom shower; split it so that 'Be in power' is the definition and 'shower' the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A monarch who reigns holds the throne, so 'be in power' is a plain verb synonym.

entries.clue: Separation, to a lion, is upsetting (9)

indicators.note: Upsetting something tips it over and jumbles it, so the letters are rearranged.

annotation.surface: Being parted from its pride distresses a lion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' reads as emotional distress for the lion, which is why it passes as part of the story.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: isolation is the state of being set apart from others.

entries.clue: Bearing gifts for the listener (8)

indicators.note: What matters to a listener is sound, so the answer is heard like the gift word.

annotation.surface: Arriving with gifts for someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bearing gifts' reads as carrying presents, as the three wise men did; 'Bearing' is a noun, meaning someone's manner or poise.
annotation.definitionFit: Bearing in the sense of dignified carriage; a person with presence has a commanding manner.

entries.clue: More coarse fish almost about to return (5)

indicators.note: Almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped.
Returning is going back, so the letters run backwards.

blocks.note: RUDD, a freshwater fish, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A coarse fish almost about to swim back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coarse fish' is an angling term for freshwater fish; split it so that 'More coarse' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Comparative adjectives: coarse language is rude, so more coarse matches the comparative form.

entries.clue: Dull relative? That is very impolite, ultimately (7)

indicators.note: Ultimately means in the end, so the last letter is taken.

annotation.surface: Complaining that a boring relative is extremely rude.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dull relative' reads as a boring family member; 'Dull' is a verb, as in dulling pain.
annotation.definitionFit: A painkiller dulls an ache, so 'dull' as a verb matches the sense of easing pain.

entries.clue: One who gives talks about parking next to European driver (8)

indicators.note: 'About' means around: the speaker word stands round the two letters.
'Next to' sets P and E side by side.

annotation.surface: A speaker lecturing on parking beside a European motorist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Driver' pulls towards cars; here it means anyone who runs a machine.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a machine, crane or train is its operator, so driver fits as a generic description.

entries.clue: Makes a request of one eating fruit? On the contrary (7)

indicators.note: Something eating takes another inside it.
'On the contrary' flips the roles, so the fruit swallows the one.

annotation.surface: Asking something of a person who is snacking on fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips who eats whom: it is the fruit that swallows the one, not the one the fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: To apply for a job or grant is to make a formal request for it.

entries.clue: Starts where thespians might be (6)

blocks.note: split into two words, this places actors on a stage or film set

annotation.surface: The points at which actors begin their work.
annotation.walkthrough: The second meaning needs the answer split in two: actors are on sets while they work.
annotation.definitionFit: Two readings: onsets are beginnings, and split as 'on sets' it places actors on film or stage sets.

entries.clue: Red mark lethal? Not half! (7)

indicators.note: Read literally, only half the word is taken: its first half.

blocks.note: a scar is a mark on skin

annotation.surface: Is a red mark lethal? Absolutely!
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', which makes the surface an alarmed answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain colour synonym: scarlet is a vivid, slightly orange shade of red.

entries.clue: Occupy Vietnam? US endeavoured, to an extent (5)

indicators.note: 'To an extent' means partly, so the answer is only part of the words that hide it.

annotation.surface: Did the US partly try to occupy Vietnam?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Occupy' looks military next to Vietnam; it means keep someone entertained.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym in the sense of keeping someone busy: toys occupy a child by entertaining it.

entries.clue: England player perhaps cheers -- not out, skipper! (7)

blocks.note: an international player is a cap, from the cap awarded
in cricket, a batsman not out is still in

annotation.surface: Congratulating an England cricket captain who is still batting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' and 'ta' are both British for thanks; 'not out' is the cricket term for a batsman still at the crease.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: skipper is the informal word for whoever leads a team or commands a boat.

entries.clue: Hide status? No time (5)

indicators.note: 'No time' means without T, so that letter comes out.

annotation.surface: Questioning whether prestige matters when time is short.
annotation.walkthrough: Cachet means prestige or status; 'Hide' is a noun or verb here, not an animal skin.
annotation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store, and as a verb to cache something is to stash it away.

entries.clue: Cook in US: I've no clue about the French type of cooking (8,7)

indicators.note: To cook the books is to tamper with them, so the letters are doctored into a new order.
'About' means around: the rearranged letters stand round the French word.

annotation.surface: An American cook admitting ignorance of French cuisine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the person in the kitchen; it is the instruction to stir the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A style of cooking rather than a synonym: the 1970s French school of light, prettily plated dishes.

entries.clue: Still following the Spanish team (6)

indicators.note: 'Following' puts the still word after the Spanish word.

annotation.surface: Continuing to support the Spanish national side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still following' reads as loyal fandom, and 'Still' as 'yet'; it is the intensifier in 'still better'.
annotation.definitionFit: A number used as a noun: football and cricket sides field eleven players, so a team is called an eleven.

entries.clue: Most of a piece of cake eaten by poor farm workers (8)

indicators.note: Most of a word is all but its last letter.
Something eaten goes inside the eater.

blocks.clueFragment: Most of a piece of cake
blocks.note: EASY (a piece of cake) without its last letter
pants is British slang for rubbish, poor

annotation.surface: Hungry labourers eating most of a slice of cake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' is an idiom for something easy, not a slice; 'pants' is British slang for bad.
annotation.definitionFit: Peasants were the small farmers and labourers who worked the land, a historical description.
